generation.hypothesis: The strength-ductility trade-off in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be overcome by engineering coherent internal boundaries at the nanoscale, such as nanotwins or nanoprecipitates, which can effectively strengthen the material while maintaining ductility.
generation.intervention: Severe plastic deformation (SPD) techniques, such as cryo-rolling or warm-rolling, followed by annealing or phase-selective recrystallization
generation.conditions: Room temperature or elevated temperatures, depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Nanotwins, nanoprecipitates, or other coherent internal boundaries
generation.mechanism: Derived from materials-science principles, the mechanism involves the interaction between dislocations and coherent internal boundaries, which can lead to dislocation dissociation, twinning, or other deformation mechanisms that enhance strength and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: High strength (~2000 MPa) and ductility (~30% elongation) can be achieved in HEAs through the engineering of coherent internal boundaries at the nanoscale.
generation.baseline: Conventional HEAs with limited strength and ductility
generation.boundary: The strength-ductility trade-off can be overcome by optimizing the processing conditions and alloy composition to achieve a balance between strength and ductility.
generation.uncertainty: The specific processing conditions and alloy composition required to achieve high strength and ductility may vary depending on the target application and material system.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructural analysis of HEA samples processed using different SPD techniques and annealing conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed HEA samples do not exhibit improved strength and ductility compared to the baseline material, the hypothesis is falsified.

Question: Can a novel hybrid-rolling process combining cryo-rolling and warm-rolling create a dual structural-compositional heterogeneous microstructure in an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy to achieve unprecedented strength-ductility synergy?. System: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA). System: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy.
